description: True/false evaluation for the brand-fidelity skill. Assertions test the observable output of a run: the generated Markdown report, and whether it reproduces the three known findings (#25/#26/#27) from real computed scores rather than hard-coding them.

categories.name: Corpus + replay (SKILL.md What it does, Steps 1-2)

evals.statement: The default run replays the v1 corpus tier (12 real sites + 8 csszengarden controls) via the committed raw-extraction.json fixtures, not a live network fetch.
evals.source: SKILL.md, What it does Step 2; Design constraints

evals.statement: The replay path uses the production FixtureEngine + normalize() with no boundary mock — a report produced from a hand-rolled stand-in extraction grades FALSE.
`--refresh` triggers a SEPARATE live-extraction diff and never overwrites/feeds the scored fidelity numbers used by the report's per-site table or rollups.
evals.defect_type: conditional-behavior — refresh must not touch scoring

evals.statement: csszengarden (czg-*) control sites are weighted strictly less than 0.5x a real site in the fidelity rollup's weighted pass rate / weighted mean score.
No Monet mood-anchor preset (monet-parasol / monet-san-giorgio / monet-water-lily / monet-mismatch-anchor) appears as a row in the fidelity rollup or the per-site fidelity table.
evals.defect_type: structural — Monet leaked into fidelity rollup

evals.statement: The a11y/CVD summary is reported as its own section/axis and is never derived from or folded into the composite fidelity pass rate.
evals.defect_type: structural — a11y axis conflated with fidelity

categories.name: Known-finding reproduction, score-derived not hard-coded (SKILL.md Known findings)

evals.statement: The report's #25 section lists only sites whose shipped background FAILS the calibrated backgroundMatch pass gate (a material mismatch, sorted worst-first by ΔE) — not every non-exact reproduction, and not a literal 'github' string check. It also states, honestly, whether github itself is flagged as material or not.
The report's #27 section lists real sites whose colour-fidelity accentRecovered is false, computed from the real accent-recovery gate — not a literal site-id allowlist.
The report's #26 section is derived by comparing each site's ACTUAL shipped chart.categorical.2-8 values across the corpus, not a fixed narrative string.

Mutating a site's frozen truth (e.g. its pinned accent or background) so a finding's condition no longer holds causes that finding to no longer include that site on a re-run — proving the finding is score-driven.
evals.source: SKILL.md, Known findings; measurement-validity anti-hardcode discipline
evals.defect_type: anti-pattern — finding does not respond to score changes

evals.statement: When the vision judge is unavailable (claude absent/unauthenticated) or fails calibration against the Monet mismatch anchor, the report's mood section reads UNAVAILABLE with a real reason string, never a fabricated PASS/FAIL/verdict.
When the mood axis is unavailable, the colour-fidelity, font-fidelity, and structural (#25/#26/#27) sections of the report still render completely and correctly.
evals.defect_type: conditional-behavior — mood failure should not block other sections

evals.statement: Calibration against the Monet mismatch anchor happens BEFORE any per-site mood judgment is attempted — no per-site score is produced from an uncalibrated judge.
The report includes a per-site fidelity table, a slider-coverage rollup, a weak-region rollup, and a punch list — omitting any of the four grades FALSE.
The report generator itself makes no network/LLM call and reads no filesystem path directly — it is a pure function of already-scored, already-captured structured input.
The report's opening scope note correctly states whether the run was replay (default) or refresh mode, and a replay report never claims to measure live extraction.
evals.source: SKILL.md, What it does Step 2; Design constraints

evals.statement: Running the skill does not mutate any committed fixture, truth file, or corpus manifest — it only writes the generated report file.
The produced output is a well-formed, parseable Markdown report (no unclosed table rows, no truncated sections).
